stages.title: Foundations
stages.description: Sound, spelling, pronouns, and who is included in the message.

stages.title: Immersion
stages.description: Hear trusted Hawaiian across short and long listening formats without turning exposure into a score.

stages.title: Sentence Patterns
stages.description: Understand how Hawaiian action patterns carry meaning, then recall and produce them.

stages.title: Comprehension in Context
stages.description: Follow who, what, when, and how parts of a sentence work together.

units.title: Foundations: Sound & Writing
units.description: Build accurate Hawaiian spelling habits, then connect them to the people and grammatical relationships that make sentences understandable.
outcomes: Recognize the ʻokina as a consonant/glottal stop
Type source-checked Hawaiian words with the ʻokina and kahakō in the right places
Notice that missing marks can point to a different Hawaiian form

lessons.title: ʻOkina & Kahakō
lessons.summary: Practice core words plus Hawaiʻi Island place names through repair, study, and recall.

lessons.title: Pronouns: Who Is Included?
lessons.summary: Learn singular, dual, and plural pronouns through repeated sentence frames, including the crucial kāua/māua and kākou/mākou contrasts.

lessons.title: Noun Phrases: One or More?
lessons.summary: Learn how ka, ke, and nā help signal singular/plural meaning and practice tracking number inside complete sentences.

units.title: Immersion: Listening Library
units.description: Use several trusted listening formats: structured lessons, short pronunciation audiograms, conversational podcasts, and the legacy HAW 101 archive.
outcomes: Become more comfortable hearing Hawaiian across different source types
Use short place-name audiograms to connect spelling with sound
Choose long-form or short-form listening without affecting mastery scores

lessons.title: Curated Immersion Library
lessons.summary: Explore structured video lessons, short UH Hilo pronunciation audiograms, learner conversation, and the HAW 101 archive.

units.title: Sentence Foundations
units.description: Build a connected grammar network: action patterns, question forms, and possessive relationships, each moving from guided understanding into retrieval.
outcomes: Recognize core action frames without forcing English tense labels onto them
Understand what information Hawaiian question forms are requesting
Track possession and participant relationships inside noun phrases
Recall familiar structures without visible choices
Transfer the same grammar into different source-checked sentences

lessons.title: Pepeke Painu: Study → Recognize → Recall
lessons.summary: Study sourced examples, identify their structure, then move into partial and full typed recall with spaced review.

lessons.title: Questions: What Information Is Missing?
lessons.summary: Learn aha, hea, wai, āhea, ināhea, ʻehia, and anei by identifying what kind of answer each complete question requires.

lessons.title: Possession & Relationships: Whose Is It?
lessons.summary: Reuse pronouns inside koʻu/kou/kona and a-class examples so possession becomes part of sentence comprehension, not a separate chart.

units.title: Comprehension in Context
units.description: Move beyond spotting familiar words. Track participants, number, inclusion, action frames, and time clues across complete source-checked sentences.
outcomes: Follow who is acting and who is being addressed
Use pronouns to understand whether a listener is included or excluded
Combine time words and action frames to infer sentence context
Interpret possession, number, and question intent inside complete sentences
Transfer familiar grammar into mixed, unpredictable review

lessons.title: Follow the Whole Sentence
lessons.summary: Use source-checked sentences to track participants, time, action, and inclusion instead of translating one word at a time.

lessons.title: Mixed Comprehension Checkpoint
lessons.summary: Mix pronouns, possession, questions, noun phrases, action frames, and context so understanding must transfer across lesson boundaries.
